title: Complementary 3D color codes for transversal quantum logic
authors: Friederike Butt, Luis Colmenarez, Erik Weilandt, Tom Peham, Robert Wille, Markus Müller
abstract: Transversal logical gates provide a direct route to fault-tolerant quantum computation, but the Eastin-Knill theorem forbids a universal transversal gate set within a single quantum error-correcting code. We propose a hybrid architecture based on the tetrahedral three-dimensional color code and its Hadamard-transformed counterpart, which we call the H-tetrahedral code. The two encodings support complementary transversal non-Clifford operations. Combined with bitwise Hadamard transformations that switch between the two encodings and a one-way transversal logical CNOT from the tetrahedral code to the H-tetrahedral code, these operations realize an almost-universal transversal logical gate set that enables both the creation of entanglement and logical states with magic. We complete a universal gate set through a pieceably fault-tolerant round-robin construction of a logical controlled-$Z$ gate between two H-tetrahedral codes. This logical entangling gate is interleaved with reduced-overhead Steane-type syndrome extraction using logical two-dimensional color-code auxiliary qubits. Our construction provides a new route toward implementing classically hard-to-simulate quantum algorithms where magic and most entangling operations are transversal while the resource overhead is concentrated in a small number of non-transversal Clifford entangling operations.
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of building universal fault-tolerant quantum computation by proposing a hybrid architecture combining two related 3D color codes. By leveraging complementary transversal operations, they achieve an almost-universal gate set, completing it through a complex round-robin construction for the necessary entangling gates. This provides a new pathway to implement hard algorithms while keeping most required operations transversal.
main_problem: Achieving a universal set of transversal logical gates for fault-tolerant quantum computation, which is restricted by the Eastin–Knill theorem.
main_result: The authors propose a hybrid architecture using two complementary color codes (tetrahedral and H-tetrahedral) to realize an almost-universal gate set, completing universality via a complex round-robin construction for the entangling CZ gate.
method: The approach combines bitwise Hadamard transformations between two related quantum error-correcting codes and utilizes pieceable fault-tolerant constructions for necessary non-transversal gates.
model_or_system: The system is based on the $[[15, 1, 3]]$ tetrahedral three-dimensional color code and its Hadamard-transformed counterpart. The implementation details involve syndrome extraction using auxiliary qubits and constructing logical operations between these two codes.
key_observables: Logical state fidelities (e.g., $F_{CZ}|\cdotangle$), effective distances ($d_X, d_Z$), and the existence of transversal non-Clifford gates.
important_parameters: The smallest instance considered is the $[[15, 1, 3]]$ code; resource overhead is concentrated in a few non-transversal Clifford operations.
main_assumptions: The initial CNOT realization between codes is one-way (control $	o$ target), and achieving full universality requires complex round-robin constructions for the missing entangling gate.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $[[15, 1, 3]]$ code structure, transversal operations in the hybrid architecture, and the ordering of physical CZ gates required for fault-tolerant logical gates.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for transversal gates, proposes the hybrid tetrahedral/H-tetrahedral architecture to achieve an almost-universal set, details the construction of the full universal gate set via a round-robin process, and analyzes related concepts like syndrome extraction overheads.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, the focus on resource optimization (concentrating non-transversal gates) and using structured codes like color codes is relevant to designing practical quantum hardware architectures that minimize error correction overhead.

(a) The X-stabilizer generators of the [[15, 1, 3]] tetrahedral color code are supported on the red (R), blue (B), green (G) and yellow (Y) cell formed by eight qubits each. Ten independent Z-stabilizers are defined on weight-4 faces within the tetrahedron. Figure 2. Transversal operations in the hybrid architecture. (a) If the control qubit is encoded in the [[15, 1, 3]] code and the target in the Hadamard-transformed [[15, 1, 3]]H code, cell-like stabilizers propagate to face-like stabilizers. This operation preserves the codespace because both control and target are a +1-eigenstate of the X-cells. The transversal CNOT gate in the reverse direction (b) does not preserve the codespace, because an X-face propagates from control to the target code that is not an eigenstate of the respective face-like stabilizer.
